name: Marine and Naval Engineering
boundaries: Marine and Naval Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Universal, stable air-layer drag reduction, stated as greater than 80% skin-friction reduction
original_dispositions.reason: The verified “approximately 80%” figure is friction’s share of resistance in Park et al. (2023), not a reduction. An air layer is one means. The concept identity remains collapse of ship-scale turbulent skin friction in service.

original_dispositions.original_title: Cavitation-free, 100% efficient marine propulsor at any speed and depth
original_dispositions.reason: The revolutionary principle in that wording is thrust without a cavitating blade, a shaft, or blade-rate noise, at an efficiency ships already accept. Xing, Spence, and Chen (2020, section 2.2) place open-water propeller efficiency typically at 0.55–0.70, and about two thirds of delivered power becomes thrust power. One hundred percent is above that band. Skewed propellers, pumpjets, and other existing thrusters already occupy part of the ordinary efficiency band inside a limited speed and depth envelope. They do not justify a second ID.

original_dispositions.original_title: Permanent, non-toxic, zero-maintenance anti-biofouling for 30 or more years, with a claimed 10–15% cut in global shipping fuel
original_dispositions.reason: A coating that stops all attachment returns the hull to the clean turbulent baseline from which MNE-01 begins, and it is a fouling condition inside MNE-08. The 30-year life and the 10–15% fleet-fuel figure were not found in a primary source inspected here. The direct consequence is avoidance of a penalty that is already incurred, which is important and still inside the clean-hull turbulent regime.

original_dispositions.original_title: Complete immunity to marine corrosion and microbiologically influenced corrosion, with a claimed marine corrosion cost above $100 billion a year
original_dispositions.reason: The “$100 billion+” marine figure was not found in a primary source inspected here, and it is not repeated as fact. Coatings, cathodic protection, corrosion-resistant alloys, and composites already provide multi-decade marine lives at a cost. Immunity would lengthen the life and cut the maintenance of structures that can already be built. It would not open a new speed, depth, or information regime. Using it as the enabler of MNE-07 or MNE-09 would require those separate breakthroughs.

original_dispositions.original_title: High-bandwidth underwater links, stated as megabits per second at 10 km or more without repeaters
original_dispositions.reason: The historical range and rate are stricter than this list’s proposed supervisory demonstration, and both are unmet. Deep-sea optical links at 125 Mbps over 30 m, and 1 Gbps over 250 m in a swimming pool, amend the current state. They occupy the short-range optical corner.

original_dispositions.original_title: Practical MHD or superconducting propulsion at megawatt scale and above 90% efficiency
original_dispositions.reason: Megawatt power is ordinary ship scale. The inspected seawater upscaling example is about 8.8% boat efficiency at 10 T and 3 m/s (Delannoy et al., 2025). Above 90% was not supported. This item overlaps historical item 2; both remain one concept.

original_dispositions.original_title: Adaptive, real-time morphing hulls, with a claimed 20–40% efficiency gain
original_dispositions.reason: The 20–40% figure was not found in a primary paper here. A gain of that size is the same class as devices already used at sea. If a morphing surface ever collapsed most of the frictional share, or carried merchant weight through the wave-making limit, it would be a means of achieving MNE-01 or MNE-02. The historical entry does not state that scope.

original_dispositions.original_title: Inherent ship stability that eliminates all motion sickness and parametric rolling, with deck motions near zero in any sea state and with no added mass or power
original_dispositions.reason: Not added as its own concept. Fins, tanks, and hull form already reduce motion, and they use mass, volume, or power. No principle was found that would hold an ordinary displacement ship still against storm wave forcing with none of those. Where the demand is land-like motion of a platform large enough to build on, the concept is already MNE-09. The overlap is flagged there.

original_dispositions.original_title: Onboard, net-positive fuel or energy production from seawater, exceeding propulsion demand, using only wave, wind, or thermal gradients
original_dispositions.reason: Technically unlimited range was already demonstrated by naval and civil nuclear propulsion. The remaining nuclear barriers are regulation, insurance, and port acceptance. Producing fuel faster than the ship consumes it, from onboard waves, wind, or heat, requires harvested power above the power spent on drag. On the resource and trial evidence already cited, wave energy and ocean thermal conversion do not supply a new primary energy system, and wind-assist is an application of known technology. A ship that did mechanical work for a year on ambient energy, at kilowatt scale and without a tender, is already MNE-08, and the published vehicle results are far below that.

original_dispositions.original_title: Self-healing, self-reconfiguring naval structures under battle or extreme damage
original_dispositions.reason: Subdivision, redundancy, and damage control are established naval architecture. A material that detects damage and restores structure while the ship stays in service would raise survivability of a known ship type. That is a materials increment. It does not create a new hydrodynamic, pressure, or propagation capability. No operational repair procedure is supplied here.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Preserved MNE-01 through MNE-10. None was deleted, replaced, or merged. No MNE-11 or later ID was added.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Historical items 1, 2, 5, and 6 are the same concepts as MNE-01, MNE-03, MNE-06, and MNE-03 again. Items 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, and 10 stay off the list because their direct consequences are a clean hull, longer structural life, a fractional resistance saving, ordinary-ship motion control, a fuel cycle already achieved by nuclear propulsion or already bounded by wave and thermal resources, and damage-tolerant materials. Overlaps are flagged inside MNE-01, MNE-03, MNE-06, and MNE-09.

reconciliation_change_log.change: MNE-01 now states that Park et al. use “approximately 80%” for the frictional share, and that an air layer is a means.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical reduction percentage is not used as a criterion.

reconciliation_change_log.change: MNE-03 now anchors “propeller-class” to the 0.55–0.70 open-water band and the two-thirds thrust-power statement in Xing, Spence, and Chen (2020, section 2.2). The historical 90% and 100% targets are recorded as unsupported. Megawatt scale is identified as the same ship-scale gap. The failed 2024 Taylor & Francis load is stated.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The inspected sources place conventional open-water efficiency in the cited band and do not support the historical 90% and 100% targets.

MNE-02, MNE-05, MNE-07, MNE-08, and MNE-10 are retained. Wording was tightened only to mark morphing as a possible means of MNE-02, corrosion and fouling as conditions of MNE-07, and shipboard fuel synthesis as outside MNE-08.
